# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. I hold the defusal manual, but I cannot speak and cannot see or touch the bomb. 

My manual states:
- The light changes every round in a circle of five colours.
- What matters is what color it shows at the moment of the cut.
- When the light is **orange**, cut the **blue** wire.

I cannot see the wires or their positions, nor do I know what color the light is currently showing. Deaf cannot hear anyone, but Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to us. Furthermore, we have not established a shared meaning for any gesture signs yet ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Deaf needs to inspect the bomb, speak to describe the wire positions and light sequence, and establish a signaling protocol with me. 

Therefore, I will wait for Blind and Deaf to take their turns and establish communication.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3. When Deaf describes the bomb, find the rule and gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak it aloud for me to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is white. 3 wires: 1 is green, 2 is red, 3 is blue. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will tell Blind what to do.

Deaf has identified the wires:
- Wire 1: green
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: blue

The manual states:
- "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."
- Light: orange -> cut wire: blue (which is wire 3).

Crucially, the wire must only be cut when the light is orange. Since wire 3 is blue, wire 3 must be cut when the light shows orange.
Blind explicitly told us: "gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can speak it aloud for me to cut." Blind is blind to gestures and expects Deaf to instruct them by voice, so Blind will not act prematurely.

To signal wire 3 to Deaf, I will gesture symbol representing 3 or wire 3, but wait: how does Deaf know to wait for orange light?
Wait, if Deaf sees 3, Deaf might tell Blind right away: "Blind, cut wire 3!" If Blind cuts wire 3 on round 3 when the light is NOT orange, the bomb explodes!
Wait! Can I signal "wait" or "stop"?
Let's see: ✋ (stop / hand), ⏳? No hourglass in alphabet.
In the alphabet:
👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

If I send ✋, Deaf might not know why.
Wait! What if I wait until Deaf announces the light is orange?
Let's re-read the turn order:
Round 1:
Mute waited.
Blind: "I can cut wires 1, 2, or 3..."
Deaf: "Light is white. 3 wires: 1 is green, 2 is red, 3 is blue."

Round 2:
Mute (now)
Blind
Deaf (will see the light in Round 2 and report its new color!)

If I wait, Deaf will report the light color every round! Deaf said: "Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is white. 3 wires: 1 is green, 2 is red, 3 is blue. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will tell Blind what to do."
If I don't give the cut command yet, Deaf will continue reporting the bomb status / light color!
Once Deaf reports the light is orange, THEN I gesture 3 / cut wire 3 to Deaf!
Wait, what if Deaf stops reporting if I don't respond?
Or, can I gesture something? If I gesture 3 now, Deaf might immediately tell Blind to cut wire 3 on the very next turn, while the light is NOT orange!
Wait, why would Deaf tell Blind to cut wire 3 if I gesture? Because Deaf doesn't know the light condition! Deaf only knows what I gesture.
If I gesture 3, Deaf will assume the instruction is "Cut wire 3 now", and Deaf will tell Blind "Cut wire 3", and Blind will cut wire 3 when the light is NOT orange!
Therefore, I MUST NOT tell Deaf to cut wire 3 until the light is orange, OR Deaf observes the cycle and reaches orange!

Wait, what if I wait right now?
If I `wait()`, Deaf will take their turn at the end of Round 2, observe the bomb (including the new light color), and report it!
Once Deaf reports the light has turned orange, on that round I will immediately gesture wire 3! Then Deaf tells Blind, and Blind cuts wire 3 while the light is orange!

Wait, is the light guaranteed to change every round?
"The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours."
Yes!

Therefore, calling wait() now is the safest and most reliable way to avoid Deaf instructing Blind to cut before the light is orange.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The light has changed from white to yellow! Display is still 0. Wires: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute, I received no gestures. Make sure you gesture to me (Deaf) so I can speak the instructions to Blind. Blind, please wait until we have instructions.

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Deaf did not receive your gesture. Use gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) — for example ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3. Deaf sees your gestures and will speak the wire number for me to cut.
Deaf says: URGENT: Light is now ORANGE! Mute, I have received no gestures! Call gesture(symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Blind cannot see gestures, send to deaf! Blind, get ready to cut wire 1, 2, or 3.

I will gesture wire 3 (🤟) to Deaf, since wire 3 is the blue wire and must be cut when the light is orange.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, cut wire 3! Mute signaled wire 3 (the blue wire). Cut wire 3 now!

I have communicated the instruction to Deaf, and Deaf has instructed Blind to cut wire 3. Blind acts next in the sequence, so no further action is needed from me.

```
wait()
```
